subject: Mutual Action Plan: hosting & region decision for Atlas Health PoC (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Nicole Tran <nicole@atlashealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:10:00Z
Subject: Mutual Action Plan & Hosting preference for Atlas Health PoC

Hi Nicole / Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I’m sharing a starter Mutual Action Plan and a concise evaluation checklist so we can align on the hosting decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and the regional constraints for the PoC. I attached: RDW_ATL_MAP_v1.pdf and atlas_eval_checklist.xlsx.

Quick summary / asks: 
- Goal: PoC (end-to-end) + performance acceptance run so Atlas can pick a deployment mode for production.
- Scope: Clinical extraction pipeline + patient-facing text generation (PHI filtered via tokenization).
- Key decision points we need from Atlas by May 10: preferred deployment mode, required region(s) for data residency, and minimum SLA for latency/uptime.

Proposed MAP timeline (draft):
1) Align on architecture and data residency requirements — complete by May 3
2) PoC kickoff (2-week) — May 10 to May 24
3) Performance acceptance run (1 week) — May 25 to May 31
4) Final hosting decision & commercial commitment — target by June 7

Notes / considerations: 
- Hosted (fastest onboarding): recommended for the PoC and early dev work. We can provision an isolated tenant in our US region with audit logs and encryption.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if Atlas needs predictable throughput and contractual SLAs; we can provide pricing/discounts tied to a 12/24 month commit.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): available for regulated modules requiring customer-managed networking or air‑gapped controls; longer lead time.

Action items for Atlas:
- Confirm hosting preference for PoC (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Share any hard constraints (e.g., required AWS region or on‑prem only)
- Return security questionnaire if Procurement wants to start review (I’ve attached a baseline we typically accept)

I’ll coordinate with Jordan and Karthik on the technical acceptance criteria and propose a one‑pager for Procurement that lays out the commercial tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated. Let me know if you want a 30‑minute exec sync next week (I’m available Tues/Wed afternoons).

Best,
Grace

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & Hosting preference for Atlas Health PoC

Internal note — drafting the technical acceptance criteria and commercial levers we should offer. Summary / recommended approach to propose to Atlas: 

Recommended staged path (minimizes risk & time to insights):
- Phase 1 (PoC): Hosted, US region (prefer us-east-1) with tenant isolation, KV + prefix caching enabled, tokenization filter for PHI. Goal: functional acceptance and basic throughput benchmarks. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (Perf validation): use Dedicated reserved capacity for a 1‑week run to validate sustained throughput and latency at target load. We can do this in the same region; Dedicated gives predictable tails and is easier to benchmark. (1 week)
- Phase 3 (Prod): choice between Dedicated or Private depending on their BAA/Compliance assessment. If Procurement needs a BAA and HSM/KMS integration inside Atlas VPC, Private is the route.

Proposed acceptance criteria (high level):
- Median generation latency < 300ms at 8 concurrent sessions
- 95th percentile latency < 850ms under target batch sizes
- Token cost within the PoC budget threshold agreed in MAP
- No unredacted PHI in logs; audit trail present for all requests
- Model quality: generated output passes Atlas product team checklist (examples attached)

Commercial levers: 
- 10% credit on Hosted fees during PoC if they commit to Dedicated within 60 days of PoC completion
- Dedicated pricing: provide two tiers (8-GPU and 16-GPU) with month-to-month or 12/24mo reserved options — I’ve attached a quick benchmark file (iops-benchmarks.csv) to help size.

Action items for Redwood: 
1) Finalize and send a short BAA/hosted-compliance FAQ to Nicole/Samir this week
2) Draft a Dedicated pricing estimate and include committed discount tiers
3) Book a joint 30‑minute technical kickoff for May 10 (proposed)

Marissa — can you pull a sample SLA and include the audit log retention options (30/90/365 days) so Procurement has what they need?

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solution Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: iops-benchmarks.csv

Grace / Nicole —

We reviewed the MAP draft and have an initial set of questions before we can proceed to legal/BAA review. I’ve attached our standard security questionnaire (Atlas_Security_Questionnaire.docx). Key asks: 

- SOC 2 report (latest), pen test summary, and remediation plan
- KMS/HSM options and support for customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private modes
- Audit log format and retention (we need at least 90 days by default; 365 days optional)
- Data deletion and retention policy for Hosted tenants
- Any cross‑tenant access controls and tenant isolation guarantees

Timing: Procurement aims to complete the security review by May 6 to keep the MAP timeline intact. Please confirm whether you can provide SOC 2 evidence and the KMS options by EOD Friday (Apr 30). Also include a draft purchase/order milestone structure so we can line up a PO if commercial terms are acceptable.

Regards,
